## `fugaro accounts ls`

List the named Claude accounts (claude_accounts in the local config) a repository may use with fugaro run --token

List the names fugaro run --token NAME (and a repository's own agent.oauth_token)
accept for a repository: "default" (the repository's own unnamed
claude-oauth-token secret, always allowed) first, then every claude_accounts
name in the local config whose allow_data_to lists the repository, sorted
(config.AllowedClaudeAccounts, the one place that decides the question).

This is a local, read-only lookup, offline whenever a project config is
already selected on this machine: it reads the local config file the CLI
would otherwise select for a cloud command, and never calls Secret Manager,
never reads or prints a token value, only names.

--json's "complete" is false when no project config could be selected for a
reason other than an explicit --config/--project/$FUGARO_CONFIG/$FUGARO_PROJECT
(several project configs with nothing to pick one, for example): "accounts"
is then "default" alone, which may be short the repository's real
claude_accounts, not a true answer that none are configured; "note" says why.

Usage: `fugaro accounts ls`

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--config` | string | "" | no | the project config file to use (default: the project's $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/fugaro/projects/<name>.yaml) |
| `--gcp-project` | string | "" | no | the GCP project ID; it must be the selected project config's gcp_project |
| `-h`, `--help` | bool | `false` | no | help for ls |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | no | print machine-readable output |
| `--project` | string | "" | no | the Fugaro project to act on (default: the checkout's fugaro.yaml project:, else $FUGARO_PROJECT, else the only project config) |
| `--region` | string | "" | no | GCP region (overrides the project config's) |
| `--repo` | string | "" | no | repository as owner/name (default: this checkout's origin) |

## `fugaro allow-delete`

Record the objects a run may delete or replace, by address (the project's owner)

Record which Terraform addresses the project's owner approves for deletion or
replacement, and which object at each address is approved, in a managed
project's fugaro/allow-delete.json at the root of the runs bucket. An approval
lives in that object and nowhere else: this command is Fugaro's only writer of
it, with the operator's own credentials.

An argument is an address and the identity of the object approved there,
written as ADDRESS=IDENTITY: the Terraform address a plan reports, as in
google_cloud_run_v2_job.web or module.web.google_storage_bucket.data,
followed by the identity a refused managed apply printed for the object that
address removes, as in

  fugaro allow-delete 'module.web.google_storage_bucket.data=type=google_storage_bucket project=proj-1234 name=data id=data-bucket'

An approval is of one object and not of the address: the same address carrying
another object later is not approved by it, so an entry an earlier apply
already used admits nothing more (the object it named is gone). The identity is
compared character for character with the one the plan's before view shows, so
copy it from the refusal rather than retyping it. Nothing else is recorded — no
note and no reason: the object's own version history is the record of who
approved what and when, and the identity is what the approved delete is
identified by.

Run it in your own terminal, as an operator, with your own credentials. Pass
the entries to approve, and they replace the list: an invocation that leaves an
entry out removes that approval, so the command names the entries it would drop
and asks for the project's name before writing such a list. With no arguments
the command prints the list — each entry in the same ADDRESS=IDENTITY form, so
a line can be pasted back — and writes nothing; it never empties the list,
because an empty list is what an absent one already means.

What the object is for: a run's own credentials cannot write it, and the
deployer account a managed apply impersonates will not be able to (D75, Task
1.5), so a managed apply can take its allow-list from the owner's object
instead of from the command line of whatever session is applying: fugaro
managed apply reads this object and takes no address flag of its own, so the
session that applies cannot widen the list. (fugaro init still honours its own
--allow-delete on its own command line, where the addresses go to tf.Guard
directly.) What this does not do: a coding agent's session holds the
operator's credentials, so it can write this object directly (gcloud storage
cp) or unset its agent marker and run this command itself. The refusal below is a speed bump against
an agent that uses the program, not a boundary against one that goes around it
(SECURITY.md records the wider Owner/Editor bypass).

On a project that is not managed, this writes an object nothing reads: the
check below is that the bucket is the project's own runs bucket, which every
installation has, not that the project is Fugaro-managed.

The list is read fail-closed: an absent object, an empty one, one naming
another project, one written by an older Fugaro (its addresses carry no
identities, so nothing in it says which object was approved), one whose fields
are not exactly the ones this command writes, or one this package cannot read
is no entries — and no entries refuses every delete and replacement rather
than permitting them. The write is fail-closed too: if the current list cannot
be read, nothing is written, and the write is conditioned on the object being
unchanged since that read, so a concurrent write is never silently overwritten
(run the command again).

Usage: `fugaro allow-delete [ADDRESS=IDENTITY...]`

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--config` | string | "" | no | the project config file to use (default: the project's $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/fugaro/projects/<name>.yaml) |
| `--gcp-project` | string | "" | no | the GCP project ID; it must be the selected project config's gcp_project |
| `-h`, `--help` | bool | `false` | no | help for allow-delete |
| `--project` | string | "" | no | the Fugaro project to act on (default: the checkout's fugaro.yaml project:, else $FUGARO_PROJECT, else the only project config) |
| `--region` | string | "" | no | GCP region (overrides the project config's) |

This command has no subcommands.

## `fugaro artifacts`

List and download what an artifact run delivered

Read and fetch the files a `mode: artifact` run put in the runs bucket.

Both subcommands read the run's result.json, never a bucket listing: ls prints
the record's own table, and get is the object — so an artifact the record names
and the bucket no longer holds (they expire with the run, runs_days) is a
recorded row that ls shows and a `get` that says exactly that.

The record was written by an untrusted, model-driven run, so get treats every
name in it as hostile: it downloads into a fresh directory it creates
(./<run>-artifacts/, with --out naming that directory's parent), refuses a name
that is absolute, walks out of that directory or begins with a dot, refuses to
overwrite an existing file without --force, and verifies the recorded size and
sha256 as the bytes arrive, leaving nothing behind when they do not match.
What it writes is never opened, executed or unpacked.

Usage: `fugaro artifacts`

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-h`, `--help` | bool | `false` | no | help for artifacts |

Subcommands:

- `fugaro artifacts get` -- Download a run's artifacts, verifying them against its record
- `fugaro artifacts ls` -- List what a run's record says it delivered

## `fugaro artifacts get`

Download a run's artifacts, verifying them against its record

Download one artifact NAME, or every artifact the record lists when NAME is
omitted, verifying each one's size and sha256 against the run's result.json as
the bytes arrive. A mismatch is an error naming both hashes, and nothing is
written — not even the file the download streamed into.

The destination is a fresh directory this command creates,
./<run-id>-artifacts/ unless --out names another parent for it. A name in the
record that is absolute, walks out of that directory, begins with a dot or
holds a control character is refused — a refusal, never a flattened name.
An existing file needs --force to be replaced.

Nothing downloaded is ever opened, executed or unpacked: the recorded content
type, the size and the sha256 are printed, and that is all. The sha256 proves
the bytes are the bytes the run uploaded; it is not tamper evidence.

Usage: `fugaro artifacts get RUN [NAME]`

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--config` | string | "" | no | the project config file to use (default: the project's $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/fugaro/projects/<name>.yaml) |
| `--force` | bool | `false` | no | replace a file that is already at a destination path |
| `--gcp-project` | string | "" | no | the GCP project ID; it must be the selected project config's gcp_project |
| `-h`, `--help` | bool | `false` | no | help for get |
| `--out` | string | "" | no | the directory to create the run's artifact directory in (default: the working directory) |
| `--project` | string | "" | no | the Fugaro project to act on (default: the checkout's fugaro.yaml project:, else $FUGARO_PROJECT, else the only project config) |
| `--region` | string | "" | no | GCP region (overrides the project config's) |
| `--repo` | string | "" | no | the repository RUN belongs to (owner/name; needed only for a bare run ID) |

Subcommands:

This command has no subcommands.

## `fugaro artifacts ls`

List what a run's record says it delivered

List the artifacts RUN (<repo-slug>/<run-id>, or a bare run ID) recorded in
its result.json: name, recorded size, short sha256, recorded content type and
the probe's verdict. The record is shown as it is — a name `get` cannot
retrieve is listed with the reason, never filtered out, and a missing object is
not ls's to hide: ls is the record, get is the object.

--json prints the record's artifact list verbatim.

## `fugaro budget`

Show and change the project's model-spend caps and kill switches

Look at and change the project's budget: the caps, today's counters, the kill
switches and the runs in flight, kept in the project's Firebase Realtime
Database (design §8). show needs the Viewer role on the Firebase project;
set, kill and resume need the budget-admin role (the project's owners and
editors, and terraform.budget_admins). preview needs the Viewer role too,
and reads the project's recipes from the runs bucket as recipes ls does,
which a plain project Viewer cannot (see docs/gcp-setup.md).

Usage: `fugaro budget`

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-h`, `--help` | bool | `false` | no | help for budget |

Subcommands:

- `fugaro budget prices` -- Show the effective model price table, offline
- `fugaro budget resume` -- Clear a kill switch (budget admins)
- `fugaro budget set` -- Set a cap, the lease limit or the mode (budget admins)
- `fugaro budget show` -- Show caps, today's counters, kill switches, headroom and the runs in flight

## `fugaro budget kill`

Halt every run of the project or of one repository (budget admins)

Set the project's kill switch (--all) or one repository's (--repo R), recording
who, when and why. Runs in flight halt within seconds (a run in its last stage
finishes pushing its work first) and new runs refuse. --all asks you to type
the project's name (or pass --yes); one repository needs no confirmation.

Usage: `fugaro budget kill (--all | --repo R) [--reason TEXT]`

## `fugaro budget preview`

Estimate a batch's worst-case model spend against today's caps

Estimate what N runs of a recipe may cost at most, and how that compares
with today's remaining daily caps. It is a ceiling, not a forecast: a run
is bounded by the smaller of budget.per_run_usd and the recipe's most
stages times the repository's agent.max_budget_usd.

That figure is the model ceiling and nothing else: a run also bills for
the machine it asked for, and no budget key bounds compute at all --
the run's own timeout is the cap.
So for every workflow the checkout defines the preview also prints a
compute ceiling -- the workflow's own resources over its own
timeouts.total, at this installation's compute prices -- and says out
loud that it is NOT CAPPED, because for a run whose expensive half is a
render on a big machine the model ceiling is not the worst case. The
basis is timeouts.total and not a render step's own timeout: a render
that overruns still burns the run's clock to the deadline. Without a
price table for the installation's region the line names what is
missing and prints no dollar figure, rather than $0.00.

When the repository's recorded runs of the last 30 days are at least 5,
the preview also prints, clearly labelled typical:, what one run of the
recipe usually costs: the mean recorded cost of each stage kind (on the
model the checkout pins for it, with the recipe's role mapping applied as
a run applies it), at the recipe's typical stage count -- one round of
each loop the recipe and its round knobs leave in, the two fix stages
sharing one mean -- over the runs of the window, whatever they ended as:
a stage counts once it recorded a cost. A kind the window has no cost
for on that model leaves the line out and names the model, rather than
pricing the pinned model with what another one cost. Runs the figure
cannot use are said to be left out, never counted as runs that cost
nothing: a run on a subscription (agent.auth oauth), whose model_usd is
notional rather than charged, a result.json that is missing or
unreadable, and a record with no per-stage cost at all (one from before
the runner kept it, or stages that all cost nothing).

The recipe resolves as it does for a run: the repository's
.fugaro/recipes, the project's published recipes, then the catalog. The
knobs come from the checkout's fugaro.yaml; without a checkout of the
repository here, agent.max_budget_usd is unknown and only
budget.per_run_usd bounds the figure, so with neither the preview says it
is unbounded.

It reads the database's caps and today's counters (the Viewer role), and
the repository's runs (the runs bucket, for the typical line). A recipe
that is not in the checkout also reads the project's recipes from the
runs bucket, as recipes ls does, which a plain project Viewer cannot
read (init removes that access): not reading it costs the project layer,
and the ceiling with it. The typical line's own read of the bucket is
the one that costs the line and nothing else: a bucket it cannot read
leaves the ceiling standing. It writes nothing.

Usage: `fugaro budget preview --recipe NAME --runs N [--repo R]`

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--config` | string | "" | no | the project config file to use (default: the project's $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/fugaro/projects/<name>.yaml) |
| `--gcp-project` | string | "" | no | the GCP project ID; it must be the selected project config's gcp_project |
| `-h`, `--help` | bool | `false` | no | help for preview |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | no | print machine-readable output |
| `--project` | string | "" | no | the Fugaro project to act on (default: the checkout's fugaro.yaml project:, else $FUGARO_PROJECT, else the only project config) |
| `--recipe` | string | "" | yes | the recipe to preview (default, lint-fix, pick, premium, review-only, solo, standard, test-and-fix) |
| `--region` | string | "" | no | GCP region (overrides the project config's) |
| `--repo` | string | "" | no | the repository (owner/name); default: the checkout's origin |
| `--runs` | int | `0` | yes | how many runs to estimate |

## `fugaro budget prices`

Show the effective model price table, offline

Show the model prices the budget accounts with: the table built into this
fugaro, its source and the day it was last checked (a warning when that is over
90 days ago), with the selected project config's model_prices applied and
marked local. A model a provider route claims is priced from the built-in
provider price catalog instead: its CATALOG column says which tier and which
end of that tier's range is charged, and the catalog has its own source, date
and 30-day staleness warning. It never reaches the network.

## `fugaro budget set`

Set a cap, the lease limit or the mode (budget admins)

Set caps in the project's budget database, with an ETag-guarded write that shows
the old and the new value.

  --global    the project's daily and per-run caps; also takes --max-reserve and --mode
  --defaults  the caps of every repository that has none of its own
  --repo R    one repository's caps

--max-reserve (the largest single lease) and --mode (observe, or enforce: caps
bite) are project-wide, so they go with --global. Amounts are US dollars from 0
to 100000, and a per-run cap may not exceed the daily cap of the same scope.
--clear removes the scope's caps.

Raising a cap (setting one that was unset counts), or lowering the mode to
observe, loosens what runs may spend, so it asks you to type the project's name
(or pass --yes). Lowering needs no confirmation.

Usage: `fugaro budget set (--global | --defaults | --repo R) [--daily USD] [--per-run USD] [--max-reserve USD] [--mode observe|enforce] | --clear`

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--clear` | bool | `false` | no | remove the scope's caps |
| `--config` | string | "" | no | the project config file to use (default: the project's $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/fugaro/projects/<name>.yaml) |
| `--daily` | float64 | `0` | no | the daily cap, in US dollars |
| `--defaults` | bool | `false` | no | the default caps of repositories without their own |
| `--gcp-project` | string | "" | no | the GCP project ID; it must be the selected project config's gcp_project |
| `--global` | bool | `false` | no | the project's own caps |
| `-h`, `--help` | bool | `false` | no | help for set |
| `--max-reserve` | float64 | `0` | no | the largest single lease, in US dollars (with --global) |
| `--mode` | string | "" | no | observe or enforce (with --global) |
| `--per-run` | float64 | `0` | no | the per-run cap, in US dollars |
| `--project` | string | "" | no | the Fugaro project to act on (default: the checkout's fugaro.yaml project:, else $FUGARO_PROJECT, else the only project config) |
| `--region` | string | "" | no | GCP region (overrides the project config's) |
| `--repo` | string | "" | no | one repository's caps (owner/name) |
| `--yes` | bool | `false` | no | confirm a raise without typing the project's name |

## `fugaro budget show`

Show caps, today's counters, kill switches, headroom and the runs in flight

Show the project's budget: the mode, the caps, today's (UTC) counted, spent and
notional dollars, the headroom under the caps, the kill switches and the runs
in flight. By default the global figures and the project config's
repositories; --repo one repository; --all every repository the database
knows. Notional is a subscription's list-price figure, never billed and never
capped. Counted is spent plus what runs have reserved and not released.

## `fugaro cancel`

Cancel a run, letting the runner open a draft PR first

Cancel RUN (<repo-slug>/<run-id>, or a bare run ID).

cancel writes the run's cancel marker; the runner sees it, stops the current
stage and finalizes a draft PR. If the execution is still in a stage after
--grace, cancel stops it through Cloud Run. It never stops a run that is
opening its PR (finalize) or writing back its cache: it waits up to 10 more
minutes for finalize, and counts writeback as finalized. --grace is never
shorter than the workflow's timeouts.finalize_reserve (5m when neither the run
nor this checkout tells) plus 40s for the runner to notice the cancel. --now
stops the execution at once (so it takes no --grace), without waiting for the
draft PR, but still not mid-finalize.

Usage: `fugaro cancel RUN`

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--config` | string | "" | no | the project config file to use (default: the project's $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/fugaro/projects/<name>.yaml) |
| `--gcp-project` | string | "" | no | the GCP project ID; it must be the selected project config's gcp_project |
| `--grace` | duration | `3m0s` | no | how long to wait for the runner to finalize before cancelling the execution (at least the run's finalize reserve plus 40s) |
| `-h`, `--help` | bool | `false` | no | help for cancel |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | no | print the result as JSON |
| `--now` | bool | `false` | no | cancel the execution at once, without waiting for a draft PR |
| `--project` | string | "" | no | the Fugaro project to act on (default: the checkout's fugaro.yaml project:, else $FUGARO_PROJECT, else the only project config) |
| `--region` | string | "" | no | GCP region (overrides the project config's) |

## `fugaro doctor`

Check that Fugaro is set up and ready, without changing anything

doctor only ever reads: the environment, Terraform, the local project config
and its installation's billing and IAM policy (with a budget backend, who can
sign sign-in tokens for it: warnings, never changes), the Fugaro plugin's wiring in
.claude/settings.json, a checkout's fugaro.yaml and its stored secrets by
name. With --check-github-app, in your own terminal, it also asks GitHub whether
each GitHub App the config records is installed on its repository with the
permissions Fugaro's runs ask for: that is the one thing that reads a secret's
value (the App's private key, with your own credentials, held in memory only to
sign, never printed), and it is refused in a coding agent's session. Otherwise
it never prints a secret's value and never creates, enables or
changes anything.

Inside a checkout whose project publishes a project layer (fugaro config
publish), doctor also names which layer applies, flags a run that launched
without it or on an older generation, a stale per-repository copy (the one
Cloud Build and the daily image check read), and a workflow whose image was
last built from settings it no longer resolves to: every one of these
degrades with a note instead of failing when the bucket is unreachable.

--plugin checks only the plugin's wiring: offline, no credentials, safe for
CI. --strict makes a stale, unpinned, foreign or unwired plugin fail the
command; the informational states ("not installed", "cannot compare") never
do, with or without --strict. A repository's CI runs
fugaro doctor --plugin --strict.

With no local Fugaro installation configured, doctor says so and names
fugaro init as the fix, rather than guessing at a project.

Exit 1 when a check fails, with the one-line fix to run.

Usage: `fugaro doctor [--json] [--plugin] [--strict]`

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--check-github-app` | bool | `false` | no | also check each recorded GitHub App is installed with the permissions runs ask for: reads the App's private key from Secret Manager with your own credentials, in memory only, for one signed token (refused in a coding agent's session; GODEBUG=http2debug would print the token, so unset it) |
| `--config` | string | "" | no | the project config file to use (default: the project's $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/fugaro/projects/<name>.yaml) |
| `--dir` | string | `.` | no | a directory in the checkout, for the plugin wiring |
| `--gcp-project` | string | "" | no | the GCP project ID; it must be the selected project config's gcp_project |
| `-h`, `--help` | bool | `false` | no | help for doctor |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | no | print machine-readable output |
| `--plugin` | bool | `false` | no | check only the plugin's wiring (offline, no credentials) |
| `--project` | string | "" | no | the Fugaro project to act on (default: the checkout's fugaro.yaml project:, else $FUGARO_PROJECT, else the only project config) |
| `--region` | string | "" | no | GCP region (overrides the project config's) |
| `--strict` | bool | `false` | no | fail on a stale, unpinned, foreign or unwired plugin (CI mode) |

Subcommands:

This command has no subcommands.

## `fugaro image build`

Build the derived image with Cloud Build; --local builds it with local Docker and smoke-tests it

Build the workflow's derived image.

Without --local, Cloud Build builds it from the repository's base branch
as the repository's build account (cloning with its bitbucket-token, or
a read-only token its GitHub App mints) and pushes it to the repository's
own registry, which fugaro init --repo creates. It pushes a candidate,
smoke-tests it without network, and only then points latest at it and
records what it was built from, unless a newer build is already
recorded. Run it from the repository's checkout: the checkout's
fugaro.yaml and origin say what to build.

A Cloud Build is billable, so it asks for the project's name typed at a real
terminal: --json, a pipe and a coding agent's session never confirm it (it
prints the one line to run in your own terminal window and exits 1).
--local builds with your own Docker and costs nothing in the cloud.

Usage: `fugaro image build`

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--base` | string | "" | no | base image (default: for a Cloud Build build the local config's base_images entry for the workflow's base, else the published fugaro-base matching this fugaro version) |
| `--config` | string | "" | no | the project config file to use (default: the project's $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/fugaro/projects/<name>.yaml) |
| `--gcp-project` | string | "" | no | the GCP project ID; it must be the selected project config's gcp_project |
| `-h`, `--help` | bool | `false` | no | help for build |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | no | print machine-readable output (--local only: a Cloud Build is never submitted with --json, nobody can type its confirmation) |
| `--local` | bool | `false` | no | build with the local Docker daemon from the checkout you are in |
| `--no-smoke` | bool | `false` | no | skip the smoke test of the built image (on Cloud Build, latest is then promoted unsmoked) |
| `--no-wait` | bool | `false` | no | submit the Cloud Build build and return without waiting for it |
| `--platform` | string | `linux/amd64` | no | image platform; Cloud Run runs linux/amd64 |
| `--project` | string | "" | no | the Fugaro project to act on (default: the checkout's fugaro.yaml project:, else $FUGARO_PROJECT, else the only project config) |
| `--region` | string | "" | no | GCP region (overrides the project config's) |
| `--repo` | string | "" | no | owner/name of the repository to build with Cloud Build (default: the checkout's origin, which it must match) |
| `--tag` | string | "" | no | tag for the built image (default fugaro-<dir>-<workflow>:local) |
| `--workflow` | string | "" | no | workflow to build; optional when fugaro.yaml defines one |

This command has no subcommands.

## `fugaro image check`

Decide whether each workflow's image needs a rebuild (the daily check; locally it only prints the decision)

Evaluate the rebuild triggers of the repository's workflows against the head of
its base branch: a blobless clone, the build record in the runs bucket, and the
base image's digest.

Run from a checkout, it uses your own git access and ADC and only prints each
workflow's decision: it never submits a build (--dry-run is accepted, and is what
it always does). Start a rebuild with fugaro image build.

With --job, as the repository's daily check job runs it (it refuses to submit
unless CLOUD_RUN_JOB or CLOUD_RUN_EXECUTION is set, as Cloud Run sets them, and
in a coding agent's session; --dry-run is always allowed), it reads the job's
spec from FUGARO_CHECK_SPEC, submits a Cloud Build rebuild when a trigger fires
(not with --dry-run), writes builds/<slug>/<workflow>/check.json, and logs one
JSON line per workflow. It exits 2 when the check itself failed.

Usage: `fugaro image check`

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--config` | string | "" | no | the project config file to use (default: the project's $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/fugaro/projects/<name>.yaml) |
| `--dry-run` | bool | `false` | no | never submit a build (locally the check never does anyway) |
| `--force` | bool | `false` | no | decide rebuild whatever the triggers say (with --job: a build is submitted) |
| `--gcp-project` | string | "" | no | the GCP project ID; it must be the selected project config's gcp_project |
| `-h`, `--help` | bool | `false` | no | help for check |
| `--job` | bool | `false` | no | run as the repository's daily check job (reads FUGARO_CHECK_SPEC; submits rebuilds) |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | no | print machine-readable output (locally; the job always logs JSON) |
| `--project` | string | "" | no | the Fugaro project to act on (default: the checkout's fugaro.yaml project:, else $FUGARO_PROJECT, else the only project config) |
| `--region` | string | "" | no | GCP region (overrides the project config's) |
| `--workflow` | string | "" | no | check only this workflow |

## `fugaro image refresh`

Move a repository onto this release's base image: pin it, point the daily image check job at it, rebuild what is stale

Run it in the checkout of an onboarded repository, in your own terminal window
(or with --yes, unattended: see below).

It prints the whole plan first, then, each step with its own confirmation:
(2) resolves this release's base image of each selected workflow's kind at
its -pinned tag, verifies its cosign signature, reads the digest back
through the installation's remote repository and pins base_images.<kind> to
it, as fugaro init --base does (nothing is copied);
(3) points the repository's daily image check job at it (its image and
FUGARO_CHECK_SPEC's base images) through the Cloud Run Admin API, with no
Terraform; (4) rebuilds each selected workflow whose build record says it
was built from another base, or that has no build record or one that
cannot be read (billable: the project's name typed for each, or --yes);
(5) names fugaro init --anchor when fugaro.yaml lacks gcp_project.

A base_images entry that is neither this release's pin nor a release image
an earlier fugaro copied (a development or hand-pushed image) stops it
before anything changes, with or
without --yes: remove the entry from the local config, then rerun. It never
writes fugaro.yaml, never onboards a repository and never runs Terraform. A
coding agent's session is refused, --yes included (there is still no --json
or --plan-only to get around that). A run that stops says which steps
finished and what to rerun, --yes included when it was given; a rerun skips
what is done. Exit codes: 0 done, 1 a refusal or a confirmation not given,
2 a cloud failure.

Unattended use: pass --yes to run it from CI or a script, with no terminal.
It confirms every step, the base pin, the check-job update and EACH
billable build, with no cap on how many builds run: read the printed plan's
build count first. --yes does not cover a coding agent's session (refused,
same as without it) or a custom, dev or hand-pushed base image (still
refused with the one-line fix); there is still no --json or --plan-only.

Usage: `fugaro image refresh`

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--config` | string | "" | no | the project config file to use (default: the project's $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/fugaro/projects/<name>.yaml) |
| `--expect-digest` | stringArray | `[]` | no | cross-check the digest of a base image's release signature, KIND=sha256:<hex>, as for fugaro init (repeatable) |
| `--gcp-project` | string | "" | no | the GCP project ID; it must be the selected project config's gcp_project |
| `-h`, `--help` | bool | `false` | no | help for refresh |
| `--image-source` | string | "" | no | the registry and owner the release base images come from, as for fugaro init (default ghcr.io/dimipaun) |
| `--project` | string | "" | no | the Fugaro project to act on (default: the checkout's fugaro.yaml project:, else $FUGARO_PROJECT, else the only project config) |
| `--region` | string | "" | no | GCP region (overrides the project config's) |
| `--repo` | string | "" | no | owner/name of the repository; it must be this checkout's origin (refresh reads fugaro.yaml from the checkout) |
| `--workflow` | stringArray | `[]` | no | a workflow to refresh (repeatable; default: every workflow in fugaro.yaml) |
| `--yes` | bool | `false` | no | confirm every step without asking (the base copy, the check-job update and each billable build, with no cap on how many run), and without a terminal: for CI or a script. The plan is still printed first. Never confirmed in a coding agent's session (CLAUDECODE and the like): nothing is applied there, --yes included. Without --yes nothing changes: a real terminal and the typed confirmations are still required, as always |

Subcommands:

This command has no subcommands.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--config` | string | "" | no | the project config file to use (default: the project's $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/fugaro/projects/<name>.yaml) |
| `--gcp-project` | string | "" | no | the GCP project ID; it must be the selected project config's gcp_project |
| `-h`, `--help` | bool | `false` | no | help for status |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | no | print machine-readable output |
| `--project` | string | "" | no | the Fugaro project to act on (default: the checkout's fugaro.yaml project:, else $FUGARO_PROJECT, else the only project config) |
| `--region` | string | "" | no | GCP region (overrides the project config's) |
| `--repo` | string | "" | no | only this repository (owner/name, as the local config's repos has it) |

Subcommands:

This command has no subcommands.

## `fugaro init`

Stand up or adopt the installation's, or a repository's, cloud resources through Terraform

init plans the installation's shared resources (the runs bucket, registries,
custom roles, the scheduler account, log isolation, an optional budget) with
Terraform, adopting what the bootstrap already made, and applies the plan it
showed once you confirm by typing the project's name (or pass --yes). It
then writes the project config from the installation's outputs. With no
project config yet, --name, --gcp-project and --region say what to create:
projects/<name>.yaml.

It enables the Cloud Resource Manager API when it is disabled (init reads
the project's number through it before Terraform can enable it), creates
the Terraform state bucket first when it doesn't exist, and offers to remove
project Viewers' read access to the runs bucket, each after its own
confirmation. --plan-only never takes --yes: what the plan needs made first
(the state bucket, the API) takes the project's name typed at a terminal, or
the run stops and says so. A plan that would delete or replace anything is
refused unless --allow-delete names the address.

A new project config grants the launcher and operator roles to you, the
authenticated user (user:<your email> from the Application Default
Credentials), so that fugaro run works; --launcher or --operator replaces that,
an existing or adopted config is never changed by it, and with a service
account's credentials it stops and names the two flags.

On a first run in a terminal it asks, once, for the project's name, the GCP
project's ID and the region, each with a suggestion (the name from the
repository's owner; the ID from GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT or the credentials' quota
project, never gcloud's default project; us-east5) and writes the local config,
so later runs ask nothing; without a terminal, or with --non-interactive,
--yes or --json, it names every missing flag in one error. Where the
installation already exists and this machine has no local config for it,
init adopts it: it writes the config from the installation and applies
nothing, and says which roles to ask an owner for. There the name is asked
after the GCP project and the region and defaults to the installation's own
(from the runs bucket's marker), not the directory's, and the budget section
(rtdb_url, firebase_project, firebase_api_key, token_signer: none a secret) is
filled from the Firebase root's outputs, read only; --name must be the
installation's name. With several project configs, --name of a project that
has none is a first run of that name, and a checkout whose origin repository
exactly one project lists selects that project.

Before the first billable image build of a GitHub repository, init asks GitHub
(as the App, with the App's key read from Secret Manager into memory only)
whether the App is installed on the repository with the permissions runs ask
for (Contents: Write, Pull requests: Write, Issues: Read, Metadata: Read): if
not, the build is left for you with each missing permission and its fix and
nothing is billed. A repository the local config does not list is asked about
first, at the start, before any plan.

init runs as a converge of stages (preflight, installation, with --firebase
the Firebase backend and the images, the secrets, the plugin wiring and the
repository), each with its own confirmation, in order,
and stops at the first that fails or needs you; a rerun resumes, and one
with nothing to do says "No changes" and exits 0. Exit codes: 0 done (or
only planned), 1 a refusal, or a step left for you (see left_for_you in
--json), 2 a cloud failure; --json prints the stages, left_for_you and the
failed stage on every outcome.

init --anchor, run in the checkout of a repository the project lists, writes
only the gcp_project: line of its fugaro.yaml (the line teammates find the
shared config from), with no Terraform, no discovery, no publish and no image
copy; plain fugaro init writes the same line as its last stage, after the whole
converge. Before it writes anything it checks, and reports together (one
line per workflow, with its fix in order), that every workflow's build record
in the runs bucket exists and was submitted by a fugaro release at or after
the one that added the field, and that the base image the image was built
FROM (the record's base_ref, whose fugaro binary the image holds) is such a
release too: a missing record, a record that does not say its base, an older
or development CLI, or an older, development or hand-pushed base fails. It
also checks that each base image the local config sets for those workflows is
this release's pin through the remote repository, or a release image an
earlier fugaro copied, at or after that release, since the next build starts
from it (a development or hand-pushed one is never replaced by fugaro init
--base or fugaro image refresh: remove its base_images entry first). The fix
it names is: that removal when needed, fugaro image refresh --repo
<owner/name> --workflow <name> in the checkout (it verifies the release's
base image and pins it by digest, points the daily image check job at it and
rebuilds the image), then fugaro init --anchor. The image checks trust the build records (written by
the builds, unsigned: the same trust as the shared config), and a hand-pushed
image under a release-looking tag passes them. Then the diff; --yes writes, a terminal asks, and otherwise it
prints the line and writes nothing. Exit codes: 0 written or already present
and safe, 1 a check failed or nothing was written, 2 a build record could not
be read from the cloud (missing credentials included). A coding agent's
session may run it, --yes included: it edits only a local file.

--forget is the rollback: it turns log isolation and registry cleanup off
with a guarded apply, then removes every address from Terraform's state,
destroying nothing else.

init --firebase <firebase-project-id> builds the project's budget backend in a
Firebase project you created and linked to billing. It may be the project's
own GCP project (one project for everything) or a project of its own (init
creates a project or links billing only with --create-project and
--link-billing, and refuses one that is missing, has no billing, or whose
database holds data and no Fugaro mark). It runs three applies, each
with its own plan and confirmation: the installation (the history account),
the Firebase root (the database, a restricted sign-in key, the token signer,
and the budget admins: the GCP project's owners and editors who are users or
groups, plus --budget-admin), and the installation again (the history job,
once its image exists). Between the last two it deploys the database's rules,
mark, project name, mode (--budget-mode; an absent one is seeded observe) and
largest lease, after a confirmation of their own, then writes the local
config. The same step creates the Firestore database for the spend history
(fugaro report) if the project has none: its location, us-east5, is permanent
(chosen once, never changed or deleted by Fugaro), so init asks you to type
the location to confirm it, at a real terminal (--yes, --non-interactive,
--json and a pipe never confirm it: the step is then left for you), and it
refuses to adopt a
database that holds data or is in another location; it also deploys
deny-everything Firestore rules and the Fugaro mark. --plan-only stops after the installation's plan. Each repository then
needs fugaro init --repo to pick up the jobs' environment.

init --repo [PATH] onboards the repository of the checkout at PATH (default:
the current directory), whose fugaro.yaml says what it needs, into the
installation fugaro init applied. It adopts what the bootstrap made for it
(checking each resource's marks and live grants first), creates the rest,
and deploys each workflow's job once its secrets are stored and its image is
built. It offers each workflow's first image build (billable: the project's name
typed at a real terminal, never --yes), then deploys the built image and unpauses the daily check. It
prints the fugaro secrets set commands still needed, and adds the
repository to the local config. A repository the local config does not list
takes the same opt-in as the converge's stages (below): its owner/name typed at
your own terminal, or --onboard-repo.

One confirmation per run, in a project Fugaro owns. A project is Fugaro's own
when this run created it (--create-project) or its runs bucket carries Fugaro's
mark (fugaro/project.json naming this project and this GCP project, in a bucket
named fugaro-runs-<gcp project> that belongs to that project; read-only check:
a custom runs bucket never qualifies). There, at a terminal, the ordinary steps (the Terraform applies of the
installation, the Firebase root, the history job and the repository, the state
bucket, the Cloud Resource Manager API, the Viewer-read removal, image copies
and base-image pins that only add tags, the Firestore marks and rules, the
local config) share one
review screen and ONE typed project name, asked when the first of them has
something to change (so a rerun with nothing to do asks nothing). Each step
still prints its own exact plan. It never covers creating a project, linking
billing, the Firestore database's permanent location, a Cloud Build, replacing
a registry tag (--replace-image), an unlisted repository or a secret: each
keeps its own typed confirmation. The state bucket and the API enable are fixed, announced, free steps; every
Terraform plan is shown as it runs and is covered only if it is creates and
in-place updates of the installation's own resource kinds, granting only the
modules' roles to the listed launchers, operators and budget admins (the review
prints them, with where each came from) or to Fugaro's own service accounts:
its attributes are the modules' (images in this project's registry, jobs of
this project, logs to this project, private buckets), and a Firebase project
other than the installation's is covered only if verified as Fugaro's; any other
plan (a destroy or replace, an IAM binding or policy, an unlisted member, a
widened role) stops that step, which asks its own typed name. A wrong name applies nothing.
The confirmation is per run and never stored. Any other project (adopted,
unmarked, or a mark that fails to read) keeps a typed name at each step;
--yes covers the ordinary steps as ever and takes no review; --non-interactive,
--json, a pipe and a coding agent never take it; --plan-only shows the review
and applies nothing.

What --yes covers: the ordinary steps, which are the installation's and the
Firebase root's Terraform applies, the images' copy, the local config's
writes, the plugin wiring and a known repository's steps. It never covers
creating a project or linking billing, a secret, a repository the project does
not list, the Firestore database's permanent location, a billable first image
build, or replacing a tag in your registry (--replace-image KIND names the
intent; the project's name is typed at a real terminal): with --yes,
--non-interactive, --json or a pipe each of those is left for you, with the one
line to run. In a coding agent's environment (CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT,
CLAUDE_CODE_SSE_PORT, CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE, CURSOR_AGENT or AI_AGENT is set) init
applies nothing, --yes included, and says to run it in your own terminal
window; --plan-only and the read-only checks still work, and so does init
--anchor (with --yes), which edits only the checkout's fugaro.yaml. That is a mitigation,
not a barrier: an agent can unset its own environment. A run that adopted an
existing installation changes nothing in the cloud in the same run (the local
config and, in a checkout, the plugin wiring in .claude/settings.json are the
only files it writes).

In a checkout of a repository of this project, the converge's secrets stage
asks, at hidden prompts, for the secrets its jobs mount (the git credential,
the Claude credential agent.auth names, none for vertex, the allowed model
providers' keys, the workflows' own), and skips what is already stored. It
prompts only in your own terminal: never with --yes, --non-interactive or
--json (--json never prompts; the stage then exits 1 with the one-line
fugaro secrets set commands), never when stdin, stdout or stderr is not a
terminal (a pipe is never read), and never when a coding agent's variable is set (CLAUDECODE
and the like; CLAUDE_CODE_SSE_PORT is also set by the Claude Code IDE
extension in VS Code and JetBrains terminals, so a person's own IDE terminal
can be refused: its refusal tells you what to do about it). A pasted private key may have at most 120 lines. It creates each
secret's container, before the repository stage, with the labels
init --repo's Terraform adopts (fugaro, fugaro_repo, fugaro_secret).
--forget removes the repository from
Terraform's state, destroying nothing.

--create-project --gcp-project <id> creates that GCP project and adds Firebase
to it, as you, after you type its ID at a terminal; --link-billing <account>
then links that billing account (it may incur charges), after you type the
account's ID. Each is its own typed confirmation, never given by --yes,
--non-interactive or --json, and the ID is never the gcloud default project.
Without --link-billing, init prints the one gcloud command that links billing
and stops. An existing project you can read is adopted; one that is held by
someone else, or pending deletion, is refused; its existing billing link is
never changed.

The plugin-wiring stage merges the Fugaro marketplace and plugin into the
checkout's .claude/settings.json, pinned to this release's tag, after showing
the diff and asking (--yes confirms it); see update-skills. The repository
stage runs init --repo for the checkout, after the secrets, when its
origin's default branch (origin/HEAD, main or master, as last fetched) has a
fugaro.yaml naming this project (else it is skipped and says why); it asks
once for the GitHub App's ID of a GitHub repository (or take --github-app-id)
and keeps its own confirmations, the first image build's included.

Both stages act only on a repository the project's local config already lists,
or one you opt in: a repository not listed yet needs its owner/name typed at
your own terminal (naming the checkout's path), or --onboard-repo owner/name,
which must equal the origin (init --repo takes both too); --yes,
--non-interactive and a coding agent's environment never cover it (the flag is
refused there), so a cloned third-party repository cannot onboard itself. The
secrets stage is behind the same gate.

Usage: `fugaro init [--repo [PATH]]`

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--alert-email` | string | "" | no | where failed image checks and rebuilds are reported (default: the local config's) |
| `--allow-delete` | stringArray | `[]` | no | a resource address the plan may delete or replace (repeatable) |
| `--allow-fork` | bool | `false` | no | let the plugin-wiring stage move the ref of a fugaro marketplace in .claude/settings.json that names a repository other than dimipaun/fugaro (a fork you host); never done otherwise |
| `--allow-job-delete` | bool | `false` | no | with --repo: lower the jobs' deletion protection, for offboarding |
| `--anchor` | bool | `false` | no | in a checkout of an onboarded repository, only write the gcp_project line into its fugaro.yaml, after checking that every workflow's job image was submitted by fugaro 0.4.0 or later and built FROM a release base image of 0.4.0 or later, and that no base image the local config sets is a development or older one (no Terraform, no publish, no image copy; the diff, then --yes writes or a terminal asks) |
| `--base` | stringSlice | `[]` | no | copy the release's base image (the only kind: base) into the project's registry now, besides what the checkout's fugaro.yaml needs (comma-separated or repeated) |
| `--base-image` | stringArray | `[]` | no | a base image the image checks run and builds start from, recorded in the local config under its base kind (repeatable; KIND=IMAGE, or just IMAGE when its repository is named fugaro-<kind>; the kinds you don't name keep theirs) |
| `--billing-account` | string | "" | no | the billing account the budget is on |
| `--budget` | int64 | `0` | no | a monthly budget on the project, in whole units of --budget-currency |
| `--budget-admin` | stringArray | `[]` | no | with --firebase: an IAM member who may change caps and kill switches besides the GCP project's owners and editors (repeatable; default: the local config's terraform.budget_admins) |
| `--budget-currency` | string | "" | no | the budget's currency, such as USD |
| `--budget-mode` | string | "" | no | with --firebase: off, observe or enforce: the jobs' budget mode in the project config, and for observe and enforce the project-wide mode in the database (an absent one is seeded observe) |
| `--check-github-app` | bool | `false` | no | let the GitHub App pre-check read the App's private key from Secret Manager with your own credentials (held in memory only, for one signed token; refused in a coding agent's session; GODEBUG=http2debug would print the token, so unset it); without it init checks only with the key you typed in this run |
| `--config` | string | "" | no | the project config file to use (default: the project's $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/fugaro/projects/<name>.yaml) |
| `--config-only` | bool | `false` | no | only write the local config, from the installation's outputs (else the flags) |
| `--create-project` | bool | `false` | no | create the GCP project --gcp-project names and add Firebase to it, as you, after you type its ID at a terminal (never with --yes, --non-interactive or --json). An ID that exists and you can read is adopted; one held by someone else is refused. Billing is not linked unless --link-billing is also given; without it init prints the one gcloud command that links it |
| `--display-name` | string | "" | no | with --create-project: the project's display name (default: its ID) |
| `--expect-digest` | stringArray | `[]` | no | pin the digest of a release image, KIND=sha256:<hex> (KIND is base or history; repeatable): the digest of the source tag's manifest (the index), obtained out of band such as from the release notes. A base kind is cross-checked against it: its digest is verified against the release's cosign signature either way, and the two must agree. For history it is the trust anchor: without it init trusts what the release tag in ghcr.io resolves to now, which is whoever can write that tag |
| `--firebase` | string | "" | no | adopt this Firebase project (the one you created and linked to billing, or created with --create-project) and build the budget backend in it: three confirmed applies, the database's rules and mark, the Firestore history database (permanent us-east5 location, typed confirmation) and the config |
| `--forget` | bool | `false` | no | roll back: turn log isolation and registry cleanup off, then remove every address from Terraform's state |
| `--gcp-project` | string | "" | no | the GCP project ID; it must be the selected project config's gcp_project |
| `--github-app-id` | string | "" | no | the GitHub App's ID, for a GitHub repository (not a secret; recorded in the local config; init asks once at a terminal, and --non-interactive needs it) |
| `-h`, `--help` | bool | `false` | no | help for init |
| `--image-source` | string | "" | no | the registry and owner the release images come from: a base kind is resolved and signature-verified there and pinned through the installation's remote repository, a history image is copied from it (default ghcr.io/dimipaun; a fork names its own, such as ghcr.io/acme) |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | no | print the result as JSON on stdout (progress goes to stderr) |
| `--launcher` | stringArray | `[]` | no | an IAM member who launches and watches runs (repeatable; default: the local config's, and for a new config you, the authenticated user) |
| `--link-billing` | string | "" | no | with --create-project: link this billing account (an ID such as 0123AB-4567CD-89EF01) to the project, after you type the account's ID at a terminal. This may incur charges on that account; never with --yes. It never changes a project's existing billing link |
| `--managed` | bool | `false` | no | with --create-project: create a Fugaro-managed project. The monthly budget amount is required — --budget, --budget-currency and --billing-account together, with no default and no suggestion taken for you — and the amount and the currency are recorded in the project's creation fact (gs://fugaro-runs-<gcp-project>/fugaro/managed.json), where a later run and a restore read what was chosen. It removes no confirmation: the project's creation still types its ID, and the installation's ordinary steps share the run's one review. Flagging a project that already exists as managed is fugaro managed flag's, run by the owner at a terminal, and never init's |
| `--name` | string | "" | no | the project's name: for a project config fugaro init creates, and what names an installation that has no name yet (with a config, it must be its name; an installation's name never changes; with several project configs it names the one to create or use; adopting an installation defaults it to the installation's) |
| `--no-build` | bool | `false` | no | with --repo: don't offer the first image builds |
| `--no-log-isolation` | bool | `false` | no | leave Fugaro job logs in _Default instead of their own log bucket |
| `--non-interactive` | bool | `false` | no | never prompt, and never read stdin: a step that needs you is listed under left_for_you (exit 1), and applying needs --yes, else the run only plans (a fresh state bucket needs its typed confirmation even then, so that plan exits 1); --yes never covers the typed-only steps (see --yes). With --forget and --config-only it only stops them prompting: their confirmations then need --yes |
| `--onboard-repo` | string | "" | no | owner/name of the checkout's origin repository (compared case-insensitively, without .git): the one non-interactive opt-in to wire and onboard a repository the project does not list yet, on github.com or bitbucket.org with an origin git config does not rewrite (--yes never covers it, and a coding agent's environment refuses it; any other origin takes the typed confirmation) |
| `--operator` | stringArray | `[]` | no | an IAM member who onboards repositories (repeatable; default: the local config's, and for a new config you, the authenticated user) |
| `--parent` | string | "" | no | with --create-project: organizations/<number> or folders/<number> to create the project under (default: no parent; an organization is never guessed) |
| `--plan-only` | bool | `false` | no | stop after showing the plan (never takes --yes: it creates nothing on a flag's word) |
| `--print-vars` | bool | `false` | no | print the Terraform variables and exit, with no cloud calls and no Terraform (ungated: no discovery, and with --repo no readiness gates) |
| `--project` | string | "" | no | the Fugaro project to act on (default: the checkout's fugaro.yaml project:, else $FUGARO_PROJECT, else the only project config) |
| `--provision-batch` | bool | `false` | no | after the installation's ordinary steps, provision the Batch compute backend into a state of its own (design docs/design/compute-backend.md §8.1 task 6): the Compute and Batch APIs, the run accounts' IAM, the launcher's, reaper's and preload accounts and roles, a Cloud NAT and router, and a preloaded boot image rebuilt on a schedule. It is money (a billable build, a NAT's hours) and permanent, so --yes never covers it and it is typed at a real terminal; nothing runs it by default, and no run can use the backend until the enable task. It excludes --repo and the flags that only read or only stop (--forget, --print-vars, --config-only, --publish-config, --anchor) |
| `--publish-config` | bool | `false` | no | publish the shared config to the runs bucket and stop (init does it after it writes the local config) |
| `--region` | string | "" | no | GCP region (overrides the project config's) |
| `--registry-cleanup` | string | "" | no | Artifact Registry cleanup: dry-run (the default), on or off |
| `--replace-image` | stringArray | `[]` | no | KIND (history; repeatable): let init replace that image's tag in your registry when it names another image, a release tag or history:latest (never done otherwise, so a hand-pushed history:latest needs it once). A base kind is refused: it is pinned by digest through the remote repository, so nothing of it is ever copied over. It names the intent only: replacing is confirmed by typing the project's name at a real terminal, never by --yes, --non-interactive or --json |
| `--repo` | bool | `false` | no | onboard the repository of the checkout at PATH (default: the current directory) instead of the installation |
| `--retire` | bool | `false` | no | with --repo: run the retirement this config change needs (a workflow or a named account removed, a secret no longer mounted): remove the protected addresses from Terraform's state (destroying nothing), apply, then delete the orphaned Cloud Run jobs through the API. The project's name is typed twice at a real terminal, and --yes, --non-interactive, --json, a pipe and a coding agent cover neither. Excludes --plan-only, --print-vars and --forget, which read or forget rather than apply |
| `--runs-bucket` | string | "" | no | the runs bucket (default: the project config's, else fugaro-runs-<gcp-project>) |
| `--scheduler-region` | string | "" | no | Cloud Scheduler region of the daily image checks (default: the region, or the nearest one Scheduler offers) |
| `--state-bucket` | string | "" | no | the Terraform state bucket (default: the project config's, else fugaro-tfstate-<gcp-project>) |
| `--yes` | bool | `false` | no | confirm the ordinary steps without asking (only after reading what they do). Never covers creating a project, billing, a secret, an unlisted repository, the Firestore location, a billable first image build or replacing an image tag (typed at a real terminal). Under a coding agent's environment variable (CLAUDECODE and the like) init applies nothing, --yes included (except init --anchor, which only edits the checkout's fugaro.yaml and honours --yes there); that is a mitigation, not a barrier: an agent that unsets its own variables is not stopped, and the real controls are the typed confirmations and the skills' lint |

## `fugaro logs`

Print a run's logs from Cloud Logging

Print the logs of RUN (<repo-slug>/<run-id>, or a bare run ID), oldest first.

With -f, keep printing until the execution ends and its logs settle. Every
line is redacted of the credentials in this environment, on top of the
runner's own redaction.

Usage: `fugaro logs RUN`

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--config` | string | "" | no | the project config file to use (default: the project's $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/fugaro/projects/<name>.yaml) |
| `-f`, `--follow` | bool | `false` | no | keep printing new entries until the execution ends |
| `--gcp-project` | string | "" | no | the GCP project ID; it must be the selected project config's gcp_project |
| `-h`, `--help` | bool | `false` | no | help for logs |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | no | print one JSON object per entry |
| `--project` | string | "" | no | the Fugaro project to act on (default: the checkout's fugaro.yaml project:, else $FUGARO_PROJECT, else the only project config) |
| `--region` | string | "" | no | GCP region (overrides the project config's) |
| `--url` | bool | `false` | no | print the execution's Cloud console link instead of the logs |

This command has no subcommands.

## `fugaro managed`

Act on a managed project (a project created by fugaro with the coding agent's refusal removed)

Act on a managed project: one Fugaro created with the coding agent's
confirmation refusal removed, where what may be applied is decided by a
deterministic gate over the saved plan rather than by a prompt.

This is not fugaro project (the project's own configuration) and not fugaro
init (which creates and re-installs an installation): a managed project's
agent-authored root is applied by fugaro managed apply.

Usage: `fugaro managed`

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-h`, `--help` | bool | `false` | no | help for managed |

Subcommands:

- `fugaro managed apply` -- Apply the agent-authored Terraform root of a managed project, as the deployer account
- `fugaro managed flag` -- Flag an existing GCP project as managed (the project's owner)

## `fugaro managed apply`

Apply the agent-authored Terraform root of a managed project, as the deployer account

Apply the agent-authored Terraform root ROOT of a managed project.

ROOT is a directory in this repository's checkout (the checkout whose
fugaro.yaml names the project). Its files are copied into this command's own
workdir — never run in place, so terraform's plan file, lock file and provider
directory are not written beside the configuration under review — the state
backend is set to the project's own managed state bucket, the root is planned
into a saved plan file, the plan is gated against the project's managed
allowlist and against the addresses the project's OWNER approved, and the saved
plan file is applied as the project's deployer service account.

An address this command may delete or replace is never one of this command's
arguments: an approval lives in the owner's object at
gs://<runs bucket>/fugaro/allow-delete.json, written with the operator's own
credentials by fugaro allow-delete. This command registers no flag for one, so
there is no way to pass one.

The refusal this command's apply does not carry is the coding agent's: in a
managed project a coding agent's session applies cloud changes with no human
prompt, and what replaces the prompt is the gate (a refused plan is not
applied), the marker (an unreadable one is not an apply), the owner's list (an
address the owner did not approve is refused) and the deployer account (which
holds no project-level IAM permission and cannot write the runs bucket). None
of the four is a boundary against a session that goes around this program.

The prompt comes back whenever the whole-project inventory does not clear the
project: before anything is planned, this command reads every resource of the
GCP project (Cloud Asset, with the operator's own credential) and compares it
with what the installation's Terraform states account for. A resource nothing
accounts for, or an inventory that cannot be read, keeps this run's
confirmation: a coding agent's session is refused and a person is asked, with
the reason printed first. Nothing is halted and nothing is deleted.

Usage: `fugaro managed apply ROOT`

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--config` | string | "" | no | the project config file to use (default: the project's $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/fugaro/projects/<name>.yaml) |
| `--gcp-project` | string | "" | no | the GCP project ID; it must be the selected project config's gcp_project |
| `-h`, `--help` | bool | `false` | no | help for apply |
| `--project` | string | "" | no | the Fugaro project to act on (default: the checkout's fugaro.yaml project:, else $FUGARO_PROJECT, else the only project config) |
| `--region` | string | "" | no | GCP region (overrides the project config's) |

Subcommands:

This command has no subcommands.

## `fugaro managed flag`

Flag an existing GCP project as managed (the project's owner)

Flag an existing GCP project PROJECT_ID as managed, recording the managed
marker in that project's own runs bucket.

This is how a project Fugaro did not create becomes managed: the marker is
what tells a later run that this project's applies may skip the typed
confirmation, and it is normally written by the run that created the project
(fugaro init --create-project --managed). Flagging is the after-the-fact way,
answered by the owner on 2026-10-16 (design D58).

Run it in your own terminal, as an operator, with your own credentials, and
type the GCP project ID it asks for. A coding agent's session is refused, and
nothing stands in for the typed ID — not --yes, not --non-interactive, not a
pipe.

PROJECT_ID must be the exact GCP project ID of the installation selected by
--project, --config or the checkout: one invocation names one project, and
there is no bulk form, no wildcard and no prefix.

It records two things in gs://<runs bucket>/fugaro/managed.json: that this
project is managed, and the monthly budget amount and currency the owner
states with --budget and --budget-currency. The amount is required, with no
default (D64), because the marker's amount is what the apply-time budget read
opens the gate on: a marked project that records no amount is refused by every
managed apply rather than applied without a budget control. The amount is the
budget ALERT amount the installation's Terraform creates and nothing else —
this command does not create or change a budget, and it makes no billing call.

It writes BOTH marks a managed project carries, in one step: that object and
the label fugaro_managed=true on the GCP project itself (Task 3.0). The read
requires both — the label is what a project can be narrowed by, and a project
without it is not managed whatever its runs bucket holds — so writing the
object alone would leave this project exactly as unmanaged as it was. The
label is written on the project, by the account running this command, which is
why the account needs resourcemanager.projects.update on it; the project's
other labels are kept. A project that already carries that key with another
value is refused rather than overwritten — the label someone else put there is
a statement, not an empty slot — and the object written first is not taken
back, so that refusal says which half is there and which is missing.

What flagging gives up, stated before it writes: the marker is what turns the
typed confirmation off (D55), so from this project's next apply on, the
deterministic gate, the whole-project inventory, the owner-written delete list
(fugaro allow-delete) and the recorded budget are what stand in the
confirmation's place — and a coding agent's session can apply a plan the gate
admitted with no human prompt.

What it does not do: it is not a boundary against a session that goes around
this program. A coding agent's session holds the operator's credentials, can
write this object directly with gcloud storage cp, and can unset its own
marker and run this command; SECURITY.md records the wider Owner/Editor
bypass. The refusal below is a speed bump against an agent that uses the
program, not a wall against one that goes around it.

A project that already records an amount is refused: the amount is the owner's
decision at the time it was taken, and this command adds a budget rather than
editing one. The one object it does replace is a version-1 creation fact —
what fugaro init --create-project without --managed leaves, and the state the
managed apply refuses for having no amount recorded. What it replaced is said
in the output, and the write is conditioned on the object it read, so nothing
is overwritten blind.

Usage: `fugaro managed flag PROJECT_ID`

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--budget` | int64 | `0` | no | the monthly budget alert amount to record, in whole units of --budget-currency (required) |
| `--budget-currency` | string | "" | no | the currency --budget is in, three uppercase letters such as USD (required) |
| `--config` | string | "" | no | the project config file to use (default: the project's $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/fugaro/projects/<name>.yaml) |
| `--gcp-project` | string | "" | no | the GCP project ID; it must be the selected project config's gcp_project |
| `-h`, `--help` | bool | `false` | no | help for flag |
| `--project` | string | "" | no | the Fugaro project to act on (default: the checkout's fugaro.yaml project:, else $FUGARO_PROJECT, else the only project config) |
| `--region` | string | "" | no | GCP region (overrides the project config's) |

## `fugaro project policy publish`

Publish the project's policy from the operator's config (budget admins)

Build the project's policy from this machine's project config — the budget
block, the providers (their secrets by NAME, never a value), the model_prices
overrides and the allow-list — and write it to config/policy/shared with an
ETag-guarded write. The diff follows the write: it is printed once the node
holds the policy, and a write that failed prints no diff — the node is as it
was, and the command says so. From then on the node is the
ceiling for every key it names, and a key it leaves out keeps the value the
job's environment was deployed with.

Publishing refuses without the rules marker (config/limits/policyRules): a
policy published before the rules are deployed is one the runs it bounds
cannot read, so run fugaro init --firebase with a Fugaro that deploys them
first. It also refuses a node written by a newer Fugaro.

allow_repos is seeded from this machine's repos: map and from the shared
config's repository list, and only when the node is absent or --seed-repos is
passed: a later publish never re-adds a name an operator removed. It is never
seeded from the bucket's runs/<slug>/ prefixes, which every run of a profile
can write.

--delete removes the policy (the children first, the shared node last, so a
launch mid-delete still sees the policy and keeps its tighter ceiling) and
puts the project back on the ceiling its jobs' environments carry. It goes
through the same rules-marker gate as a publish, refuses without --yes while
runs are in flight, and asks you to type the project's name otherwise. The
config/policy/repos children are removed too, shared node or not: a delete
that failed on the shared node leaves them behind, and this is what clears
them.

routing.claude is written where the operator writes it: this config. A publish
refuses to drop an active route the config does not account for, and refuses
a config that writes a routing block naming no Claude switch in the same
state; --remove-routing is how the operator says the block goes away on
purpose.

Usage: `fugaro project policy publish [--seed-repos] [--delete] [--yes] [--remove-routing]`

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--config` | string | "" | no | the project config file to use (default: the project's $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/fugaro/projects/<name>.yaml) |
| `--delete` | bool | `false` | no | remove the published policy (project-centric mode off again) |
| `--gcp-project` | string | "" | no | the GCP project ID; it must be the selected project config's gcp_project |
| `-h`, `--help` | bool | `false` | no | help for publish |
| `--project` | string | "" | no | the Fugaro project to act on (default: the checkout's fugaro.yaml project:, else $FUGARO_PROJECT, else the only project config) |
| `--region` | string | "" | no | GCP region (overrides the project config's) |
| `--remove-routing` | bool | `false` | no | drop the published policy's routing block on purpose (an active route stops being taken) |
| `--seed-repos` | bool | `false` | no | seed allow_repos from the operator's repositories again |
| `--yes` | bool | `false` | no | confirm the deletion without typing the project's name |

Subcommands:

This command has no subcommands.

## `fugaro project repos rm`

Un-enroll a repository: remove it from the allow-list

Remove an entry from the published policy's allow_repos. Removing an allowed
repository stops its runs — a run of a repository the list does not admit is
refused before it mints a git token — unless another entry on the list still
admits it, which is the case a pattern makes (github/acme/app stays admitted
while github/acme/* is there); the confirmation says which of the two it is.
Removing * refuses every repository the rest of the list does not admit.
So it asks you to type the project's name, and while a run is in flight --yes
alone is not enough.

Usage: `fugaro project repos rm <provider/owner/name | owner/name | *>`

| `--gcp-project` | string | "" | no | the GCP project ID; it must be the selected project config's gcp_project |

## `fugaro report`

Report what the project spent, by day, week, month, year, repository, model or person

Report model spend from the project's spend history.

Finished days are read from the spendDaily documents in the project's Firebase
Firestore (you need roles/datastore.viewer on the Firebase project, which
launchers, operators and budget admins have). Today, yesterday and any day the
daily job has not archived yet are computed live from the budget database and
marked (partial). --since and --until are UTC dates (YYYY-MM-DD); --since also
takes Nd, the last N days up to --until (default 30d); --until defaults to today.

--by day|week|month|year groups in time; weeks are ISO weeks in UTC, starting on
Monday (2026-W40). --by repo|model|person groups across the range. Dollars are
exact (integer micro-dollars). Model $, NOTIONAL~ (a subscription's list-price
figure, never billed) and COMPUTE $ are separate columns and never summed;
compute reads n/a when no run's compute was estimated. A person is the stored
requester address; `unknown` is spend, and runs, with no requester recorded.
By model, a subscription model's dollars are notional (priced from its tokens,
so they can differ slightly from the run's recorded notional total).

--csv writes RFC 4180 with spreadsheet-safe cells (a cell starting with = + - @
is prefixed with '). --json prints {project, source, degraded, by, since, until,
weeks, rows[{key, start, end, partial, model_micros, model_usd, notional_micros,
notional_usd, compute_micros, compute_usd, compute_estimated, run_hours, runs,
calls, tokens}], totals, warnings}; *_usd are exact decimal strings and null
means n/a or not recorded for that breakdown.

A project without Firestore history says so and shows run-record totals instead
(from the runs bucket, not budget history).

Usage: `fugaro report`

Flags:

| Flag | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--by` | string | `day` | no | group by day, week, month, year, repo, model or person |
| `--config` | string | "" | no | the project config file to use (default: the project's $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/fugaro/projects/<name>.yaml) |
| `--csv` | bool | `false` | no | print CSV (RFC 4180) |
